result:
The proposed answer of 5 is probably wrong.

The solution does not actually carry out the classification. It asserts "systematic analysis" and an "exhaustive verification" without giving any argument. Its table also hedges on whether Q(C₃) differs from V(C₃), which shows the case analysis was not done.

Its structural claims are also doubtful. The variety chain is presented without care for which C_n embed into which, and the quasivarieties between varieties are never identified.

My recollection of the literature is that the number of Sugihara-algebra quasivarieties with the amalgamation property is larger than 5, around 20. I am not certain of the exact figure, but I am fairly confident it is not 5.

VERDICT: REJECT
